title.zh: 中医美白淡斑：内调外治的自然美白法
title.en: TCM Whitening & Spot Removal: Natural Brightening from Within

description.zh: 掌握中医美白淡斑的方法，从内调理气血，外用中药面膜，实现自然美白
description.en: Master TCM whitening methods, regulate Qi-Blood internally, use herbal masks externally

zh.text: 美白和淡斑是许多人护肤的核心诉求，但市面上众多美白产品往往让人眼花缭乱，效果却不尽如人意。从中医的角度来看，面色暗沉和色斑的形成绝非单纯的皮肤问题，而是体内脏腑功能失调的外在投射。《素问·上古天真论》指出："女子五七，阳明脉衰，面始焦，发始堕。"这不仅说明面色变化与经脉气血的盛衰直接相关，更启示我们——真正的美白不是漂白肤色，而是通过调理内在的气血、肝、脾、肾，让皮肤自然而然地恢复健康的色泽。本文从内调外治两个维度，系统介绍中医美白淡斑的思路和方法。
色斑形成的原因
中医将色斑统称为"黧黑斑"或"面尘"，其病机核心在于"气血失和、瘀浊停留"。具体而言，肝、脾、肾三脏的功能失调是色斑产生的内在根源。《医宗金鉴·外科心法要诀》总结道："黧黑斑始生面上，由忧思抑郁，血弱不华，以致火燥结成斑黑。"这段论述精辟地概括了色斑形成的情志、气血和火热三方面因素。
肝郁气滞
肝郁气滞是黄褐斑最常见的中医证型，尤其在女性患者中占比极高。《灵枢·经脉》说："肝足厥阴之脉……上出额，与督脉会于巅。"肝气郁结则气血运行不畅，面部气血瘀滞，日久便会形成黄褐斑。这类患者往往情绪敏感、容易焦虑或易怒，色斑在经前加重、经后减轻，常伴有乳房胀痛、月经不调等表现。我在临床中对这类患者的处理原则是"欲治其斑，先疏其肝"，逍遥散为基础方加减，配合玫瑰花、佛手等疏肝理气之品，往往效果显著。
气血不足
气血不足所致的面色暗沉在临床上也十分常见。《难经》云："气主煦之，血主濡之。"气血亏虚则面部失于温煦和濡养，面色萎黄无华、皮肤粗糙不泽。这类患者不仅面色差，还常伴有神疲乏力、头晕心悸、月经量少色淡等全身性的气血不足表现。调理重点在于补益气血，八珍汤是气血双补的经典方，日常食疗可常食当归、黄芪、红枣、桂圆等。
脾胃虚弱
脾胃为后天之本、气血生化之源。《素问·五脏生成》说："脾之合肉也，其荣唇也。"脾虚则运化失常，水湿内停，湿浊上泛于面，可表现为面色萎黄、面部浮肿和色斑。这类患者常伴有食欲不振、腹胀便溏、舌胖有齿痕等脾虚之象。调理需从健脾入手，参苓白术散是健脾祛湿的代表方。日常可多食山药、薏米、茯苓等健脾食材。
肾虚
肾虚导致的色斑多见于中老年人群或长期熬夜、过度劳累者。肾藏精，其华在发，肾精不足则面色失养，出现色素沉着。《素问·上古天真论》以肾气盛衰描述人体的生长衰老过程，肾精亏耗则"面焦发堕"。这类色斑颜色偏暗、范围较广，患者常伴有腰膝酸软、头晕耳鸣、记忆力减退等肾虚表现。调理应以补肾填精为主，六味地黄丸为基础方，可配合枸杞、桑葚、黑芝麻等食疗。
内调美白方法
内调是中医美白的根本，只有脏腑功能协调、气血充足通畅，面色才能由内而外地焕发光彩。以下从三个主要证型出发介绍内调方法。
疏肝解郁
疏肝解郁是调理肝郁型面色暗沉的核心方法。玫瑰花茶是最简便的日常选择，玫瑰花疏肝理气、活血化瘀，每日取5至8朵泡水代茶饮，长期坚持可见面色改善。菊花茶清肝明目，搭配枸杞效果更佳。如果色斑较为顽固，可选用柴胡疏肝散等经典方剂进行系统调理。太冲穴是肝经原穴，位于足背第一、二跖骨结合部前方凹陷中，每日按揉3至5分钟，有助于疏解肝气、改善面部气血。
补气养血
补气养血是改善气血不足型面色的关键。当归是补血第一要药，兼具活血之功，让新血得生、旧血得行。《本草纲目》称其"治头痛、心腹诸痛，润肠胃筋骨皮肤"，是美白养颜不可或缺的药材。黄芪补气升阳，与当归配伍即经典名方"当归补血汤"，体现了"气能生血"的中医理论。红枣补气养血，性质温和，适合长期食用。阿胶补血滋阴，适合血虚明显的患者，但需注意阿胶滋腻碍胃，脾胃虚弱者不宜大量使用。
健脾祛湿
健脾祛湿适用于脾虚湿盛型的面色暗沉。薏米在《本草纲目》中记载"健脾益胃，补肺清热，去风胜湿"，是健脾祛湿的常用食材，可煮粥或煮水代茶。茯苓健脾利湿而不伤正，山药健脾益气，白术健脾燥湿。四味合用，是健脾祛湿、改善面色的经典组合。我常建议患者用薏米、山药、茯苓、莲子煮粥作为早餐，长期食用后不仅面色改善，整个人的消化功能和体力也会同步提升。
经典美白方剂
三白汤
三白汤是古代最著名的美白内服方之一，由白芍、白术、白茯苓三味组成，药名皆带"白"字，寄寓"以白养白"之意。白芍养血柔肝、敛阴和营，白术健脾益气、燥湿利水，白茯苓健脾利湿、宁心安神。三药合用，从养血、健脾、利湿三个角度综合调理，适用于气血失调、脾虚湿盛所致的面色暗沉和黄褐斑。我在临床中常在此方基础上加入甘草调和诸药，并可根据患者实际情况增减当归、川芎等养血活血之品。
玉容散
玉容散是古代宫廷美容外用的经典洗面方，由白芷、白术、白茯苓、白芍、白及等组成。方中各药多为白色，取"白色入肺、肺主皮毛"之义。白芷辛温芳香，可"长肌肤、润泽颜色"；白术健脾燥湿；白茯苓健脾利湿；白芍养血柔肝；白及收敛止血、生肌敛疮。玉容散研末后调水洗面或做面膜，对于面色暗沉、黄褐斑和皮肤粗糙都有较好的改善效果。需要注意的是，白芷含有光敏成分，使用后应注意防晒。
外用美白方法
中药面膜

外用中药面膜是美白淡斑最直接的方法。珍珠粉面膜以其美白细腻肌肤的功效流传千年，《本草纲目》记载珍珠"涂面，令人润泽好颜色"。白芷面膜以白芷粉调蜂蜜外敷，对色素沉着有较好的淡化作用，但需注意避光。当归面膜适合面色萎黄、气血不足者，取当归粉调蜂蜜敷面，每周2至3次。三白粉面膜（白芷、白术、白茯苓）是最经典的美白面膜方，适用于大多数肤质，根据干油性调整调液即可。这些面膜虽然效果温和，贵在坚持，通常使用一个月以上开始见到肤色提亮的效果。
美白穴位按摩
面部穴位按摩可有效改善局部气血循环，辅助美白淡斑。四白穴是面部美白第一要穴，每日按揉以酸胀为度。迎香穴在鼻翼旁，按揉可改善整体面色。太阳穴按揉能促进面部气血运行。颧髎穴在颧骨下缘凹陷处，按揉可淡化色斑。这些穴位每日按揉3至5分钟，长期坚持对改善面色和淡化色斑有积极的辅助作用。但需认识到，穴位按摩是辅助手段，对于顽固色斑需要配合内调才能从根本上解决问题。

zh.title: 三白美白茶
zh.instructions:
1. 所有材料洗净
2. 加水煮沸
3. 转小火煮15分钟
4. 代茶饮用
5. 每日1次，连续饮用
6. 美白淡斑，调和气血

zh.text: 美白生活习惯

美白是一项系统工程，生活习惯的影响不容低估。防晒是所有美白工作的前提——紫外线不仅会晒黑皮肤，更是色斑形成和加深的首要外部因素。无论晴雨，出门都应涂抹防晒霜或采取物理防晒措施。充足的睡眠是皮肤修复的黄金时间，晚上11点至凌晨3点的深度睡眠最有利于皮肤细胞的新陈代谢和修复。情绪舒畅对肝郁型色斑的改善至关重要，长期的焦虑和压抑会直接导致肝气郁结、面部气血瘀滞。饮食上应多摄入富含维生素C的蔬果（如猕猴桃、西红柿、橙子），以及具有抗氧化作用的食物（如绿茶、蓝莓）。多喝水促进代谢和毒素排出，对维持皮肤通透感也有帮助。
温馨提示：美白淡斑需要长期坚持，不可急于求成。本文所介绍的方法仅供日常调理参考。色斑严重或短期内迅速增多、颜色加深者，建议先到正规医院皮肤科确诊，排除其他皮肤病变后再行中医调理。建议在专业中医师辨证指导下进行综合治疗。

en.text: Whitening and spot fading are core skincare goals for many people, yet the bewildering array of commercial whitening products often delivers disappointing results. From a TCM perspective, dull complexion and pigmentation are not merely skin issues but external manifestations of internal organ dysfunction. The Su Wen states: "At age 35 for women, the yangming meridian declines, the face begins to wither, and hair begins to fall." This reveals that complexion changes are directly linked to the abundance or decline of qi and blood in the meridians, and more importantly, it teaches us that true whitening is not about bleaching the skin but about harmonizing the internal qi, blood, liver, spleen, and kidney so that the skin naturally recovers a healthy complexion. This article presents a systematic TCM approach to whitening and spot fading from both internal regulation and external treatment perspectives.
Causes of Spots Formation

TCM classifies pigmentation spots as "dark patches" or "facial dust," with the core pathogenesis being "disharmony of qi and blood with stagnation of turbidity." Specifically, dysfunction of the liver, spleen, and kidney forms the internal basis for spot formation. The Golden Mirror of Medicine summarizes: "Dark patches arise on the face from worry, thought, and depression, with weakened blood failing to nourish, resulting in fire-dryness that congeals into spots." This passage incisively encapsulates the emotional, qi-blood, and heat factors involved in spot formation.
Liver Stagnation

Liver qi stagnation is the most common TCM pattern of melasma, particularly prevalent among female patients. The Lingshu states: "The foot jueyin liver meridian... ascends to the forehead and meets the du meridian at the vertex." When liver qi becomes constrained, qi and blood circulation is impaired, leading to stagnation on the face that eventually forms melasma. These patients are typically emotionally sensitive, prone to anxiety or irritability, and their spots worsen before menstruation and improve after, often accompanied by breast distension and menstrual irregularities. My clinical approach for these patients follows the principle: "to treat the spots, first soothe the liver." Using Xiao Yao San as the base formula with modifications, supplemented with rose and bergamot to soothe the liver and regulate qi, typically yields significant results.
Qi-Blood Deficiency

Dull complexion due to qi-blood deficiency is also commonly encountered clinically. The Nan Jing states: "Qi warms, blood nourishes." When qi and blood are deficient, the face loses warmth and nourishment, appearing sallow, lusterless, and rough. These patients not only have a poor complexion but also present with systemic signs of qi-blood deficiency such as fatigue, dizziness, palpitations, and scanty, pale menstruation. The treatment focus is on tonifying qi and blood. Ba Zhen Tang (Eight Precious Decoction) is the classic formula for dual qi-blood tonification. Daily dietary therapy may include angelica, astragalus, red dates, and longan.
Spleen Weakness

The spleen is the foundation of acquired constitution and the source of qi and blood production. The Su Wen states: "The spleen's corresponding tissue is muscle, and its brilliance manifests on the lips." Spleen deficiency impairs transportation and transformation, leading to internal water-dampness retention that rises to the face, manifesting as sallow complexion, facial puffiness, and spots. These patients often present with poor appetite, abdominal distension, loose stool, and a swollen tongue with tooth marks. Treatment should begin with strengthening the spleen. Shen Ling Bai Zhu San is a representative formula for strengthening the spleen and resolving dampness. Daily foods such as yam, coix seed, and poria are recommended.
Kidney Deficiency

Kidney deficiency-related pigmentation is more commonly seen in middle-aged and elderly individuals or those with chronic sleep deprivation and overexertion. The kidney stores essence, and its brilliance manifests in the hair — when kidney essence is insufficient, the face loses nourishment, and pigmentation develops. The Su Wen describes the human growth and aging process through the waxing and waning of kidney qi: kidney essence depletion leads to "facial withering." These spots tend to be darker in color and cover a wider area, accompanied by lower back soreness, dizziness, tinnitus, and memory decline. Treatment should focus on supplementing kidney essence. Liu Wei Di Huang Wan is the base formula, supplemented with goji berries, mulberries, and black sesame as dietary therapy.
Internal Whitening Methods

Internal regulation is the foundation of TCM whitening. Only when organ functions are harmonious and qi and blood are abundant and flowing can the complexion radiate from within. The following internal regulation methods address three primary patterns.
Soothe Liver, Resolve Stagnation

Soothing the liver and resolving stagnation is the core method for treating liver stagnation-type dull complexion. Rose tea is the simplest daily choice — rose flowers soothe the liver and regulate qi while activating blood circulation. Steep 5 to 8 buds as tea daily, and consistent use will gradually improve complexion. Chrysanthemum tea clears the liver and brightens the eyes, with even better results when paired with goji berries. For more stubborn pigmentation, classic formulas such as Chai Hu Shu Gan San may be used for systematic regulation. Taichong (LV3), the source point of the liver meridian located on the dorsum of the foot in the depression anterior to the junction of the first and second metatarsal bones, should be massaged for 3 to 5 minutes daily to help soothe liver qi and improve facial circulation.
Tonify Qi-Blood

Tonifying qi and blood is essential for improving qi-blood deficiency-type complexion. Angelica sinensis is the foremost blood-tonifying herb with the additional property of activating blood circulation, enabling both the generation of new blood and the movement of existing blood. The Ben Cao Gang Mu describes it as "treating headaches and various abdominal pains, moistening the intestines, bones, and skin" — making it an indispensable herb for whitening and beauty. Astragalus tonifies qi and raises yang, and when paired with angelica, it forms the classic formula "Dang Gui Bu Xue Tang" (Angelica Blood-Tonifying Decoction), embodying the TCM principle that "qi generates blood." Red dates tonify qi and blood with gentle properties suitable for long-term use. Donkey-hide gelatin tonifies blood and nourishes yin, suitable for patients with pronounced blood deficiency, though its richness may impair digestive function in those with weak spleens.
Strengthen Spleen, Resolve Dampness

Strengthening the spleen and resolving dampness is the approach for spleen deficiency with dampness-type dull complexion. Coix seed is recorded in the Ben Cao Gang Mu as "strengthening the spleen and stomach, tonifying the lung and clearing heat, dispelling wind and resolving dampness" — it can be cooked as porridge or boiled as tea. Poria strengthens the spleen and drains dampness without damaging the righteous qi. Yam strengthens the spleen and tonifies qi. Atractylodes strengthens the spleen and dries dampness. The combination of these four herbs forms a classic formula for strengthening the spleen, resolving dampness, and improving complexion. I often recommend patients cook a breakfast porridge with coix seed, yam, poria, and lotus seeds. After prolonged consumption, not only does the complexion improve, but digestive function and overall energy levels also rise simultaneously.
Classic Whitening Formulas
San Bai Tang (Three Whites Decoction)

San Bai Tang is one of the most famous ancient internal whitening formulas, composed of White Peony, White Atractylodes, and White Poria — each ingredient containing the character for "white," embodying the concept of "nourishing whiteness with white." White Peony nourishes blood and softens the liver, constrains yin and harmonizes the nutritive level. White Atractylodes strengthens the spleen, tonifies qi, dries dampness, and promotes urination. White Poria strengthens the spleen, drains dampness, and calms the spirit. The combination regulates from three angles — nourishing blood, strengthening the spleen, and draining dampness — making it suitable for dull complexion and melasma due to qi-blood disharmony and spleen deficiency with dampness. In clinical practice, I add licorice to harmonize the ingredients and may incorporate angelica and chuanxiong to nourish and activate blood based on the patient's specific condition.
Yu Rong San (Jade Face Powder)

Yu Rong San is a classic ancient palace external beauty wash formula composed of Angelica dahurica, Atractylodes, Poria, White Peony, and Bletilla. Most ingredients are white in color, following the principle of "white enters the lung, the lung governs the skin." Angelica dahurica, acrid, warm, and aromatic, can "nourish the skin and improve complexion." Atractylodes strengthens the spleen and dries dampness. Poria strengthens the spleen and drains dampness. White Peony nourishes blood and softens the liver. Bletilla constrains blood, generates tissue, and heals sores. When ground into fine powder and mixed with water for face washing or mask application, Yu Rong San effectively improves dull complexion, melasma, and rough skin. It should be noted that Angelica dahurica contains photosensitizing compounds, so sun protection is necessary after use.
External Whitening Methods
Herbal Masks

External herbal masks are the most direct method for whitening and spot fading. Pearl powder mask has been used for millennia for whitening and refining skin texture — the Ben Cao Gang Mu records that pearl "when applied to the face, improves complexion." Angelica dahurica mask, made by mixing the powder with honey and applying externally, effectively fades pigmentation, though sun protection is required. Angelica mask suits those with sallow complexion due to qi-blood deficiency — mix angelica powder with honey and apply 2 to 3 times weekly. San Bai powder mask (Angelica dahurica, Atractylodes, Poria) is the most classic whitening mask formula, suitable for most skin types with the mixing medium adjusted for dry or oily skin. While the effects of these masks are gentle, consistency is key — improvement in skin brightness typically becomes noticeable after one month of regular use.
Whitening Acupoint Massage

Facial acupoint massage effectively improves local qi and blood circulation, supporting whitening and spot-fading efforts. Sibai (ST2) is the foremost facial whitening point — massage daily until a sensation of soreness and distension is felt. Yingxiang (LI20), beside the nasal ala, improves overall complexion when pressed. Taiyang (EX-HN5) massage promotes facial qi and blood circulation. Quanliao (SI18), in the depression below the cheekbone, helps fade pigmentation when massaged. Massaging these points for 3 to 5 minutes daily provides positive support for improving complexion and fading spots over the long term. However, it must be recognized that acupoint massage is an辅助 measure — stubborn pigmentation requires internal regulation to fundamentally resolve the problem.

en.title: San Bai Whitening Tea
en.instructions:
1. Wash all ingredients
2. Boil water
3. Simmer for 15 minutes
4. Drink as tea
5. Once daily, continuous use
6. Whitens, fades spots, harmonizes Qi-Blood

en.text: Whitening Lifestyle Habits

Whitening is a systematic endeavor in which the influence of lifestyle habits cannot be underestimated. Sun protection is a prerequisite for all whitening efforts — UV radiation not only tans the skin but is the primary external factor in spot formation and deepening. Sunscreen or physical sun protection measures should be used whenever going outside, regardless of weather. Adequate sleep is the golden time for skin repair — deep sleep between 11 PM and 3 AM is most beneficial for skin cell metabolism and repair. Emotional well-being is critical for improving liver stagnation-type spots — chronic anxiety and suppression directly lead to liver qi constraint and facial qi-blood stasis. The diet should emphasize vitamin C-rich fruits and vegetables (such as kiwi, tomatoes, and oranges) and antioxidant-rich foods (such as green tea and blueberries). Adequate water intake promotes metabolism and toxin elimination, helping maintain skin clarity.

Note: Whitening and spot fading require long-term commitment and patience. The methods described in this article are for daily health maintenance reference only. Those with severe pigmentation or rapidly increasing, darkening spots should first consult a dermatologist at a正规 hospital to rule out other skin pathology before pursuing TCM treatment. Comprehensive treatment under the guidance of a qualified TCM practitioner is recommended.
